kurz: Which problem the blockchain solves, which function of money Bitcoin does not fulfil and which figures matter when assessing crypto-assets.

bloecke.md:
A [[blockchain]] is a ledger of which every participant holds a complete copy. Each block contains the cryptographic fingerprint of the previous block. If an old entry is changed, all later fingerprints change, and the change is noticed immediately. The technology thus solves a single problem: the double spending of the same balance. A file can be copied at will, whereas a balance may only be spent once. Until now, this was ensured by a central body that keeps the only valid ledger, such as a bank, a central bank or a register. Bitcoin replaces this body with a rule that is cheaper for the participants to comply with than to break.

This requires redundancy. Every payment is stored and verified by thousands of computers. A system that is meant to work without trust in a central body has to replace this trust with effort, and this effort costs money. All further statements about cryptocurrencies no longer concern the technology; they are interpretation.

## Consensus mechanisms

With [[proof of work]], computers try out numbers billions of times until the fingerprint of a block falls below a target value. The computer that finds a suitable number first appends the next block and receives the reward. The difficulty is adjusted every 2,016 blocks so that on average one block is created every ten minutes, regardless of how much computing power is in the network. An attack is therefore prevented by the electricity costs it would incur. According to a 2025 study by the University of Cambridge, the Bitcoin network consumed around 0.5% of the world's electricity and caused around 0.08% of global greenhouse gas emissions. This corresponds roughly to the annual emissions of Slovakia.

With [[proof of stake]], a pledged deposit takes the place of computing power. Ethereum switched to this method on 15 September 2022 (“The Merge”) and reduced its energy consumption by around 99%. Anyone who wants to validate transactions deposits 32 ETH. In the event of fraud or persistent downtime, part of this is lost. The reward in September 2026 was around 2.6% a year. This is not interest in the usual sense. The amount comes from newly issued coins, transaction fees and priority rights when ordering transactions, and is paid out in ETH. The price of ETH can halve while the percentage stays the same.

The limit of 21 million is a protocol rule and not a law of nature. It applies to Bitcoin, not to the asset class as a whole. In September 2026, around 13,100 crypto-assets were listed. The quantity of a single protocol is limited, but the number of protocols is not.

Every 210,000 blocks, that is roughly every four years, the reward halves. At ten minutes per block, that is about 52,560 blocks a year. The table relates the resulting inflow to the existing supply of around 19.99 million BTC in February 2026, which is 95.2% of the final quantity. Scarcity has therefore essentially already been reached. The 2028 [[halving]] reduces the annual new inflow from around 0.8% to around 0.4% of the existing supply. Gold mines, by contrast, produce around 1.7% of the above-ground gold stock every year.

The date has been in the code since 2009. According to standard market theory, an event that all market participants know about years in advance is priced in before it occurs. A price pattern derived from the previous four halvings is based on only four observations. That is not enough for a statistical statement.

## Bitcoin and the functions of money

Whether something is money is decided by use and not by a manifesto. Three functions have to be examined, and Bitcoin fulfils them to different degrees.

Prices that mean the same over weeks
Not fulfilled. Wages, rents and prices of goods are calculated in euros, even by Bitcoin holders.

Disputed. Over twelve years far higher returns than the stock market; from October 2025 to June 2026 a fall of 53%.

bloecke.md: An average of this series does not describe an outcome that any investor has experienced. Every return figure therefore depends almost entirely on the starting year. Anyone who quotes a figure is, by choosing the starting year, also choosing the result.

bloecke.md: Over the entire period since 2014, Bitcoin's annual volatility was around 67%, roughly four times that of the equity index and gold. This also affects the diversification argument. An addition to a portfolio only helps if it performs differently from the rest of the portfolio, above all in crises.

bloecke.unter: Pearson correlation of daily returns. Co-movement has increased since the same investors started holding both. The benefit for diversification is therefore not constant and is declining.

bloecke.md: The argument is that the limited supply protects against currency debasement. It was put to the test in 2022. The German inflation rate averaged 6.9% for the year, higher than it had been for decades. Bitcoin lost 64% in the same year. In the correction from October 2025, Bitcoin fell by 53%, while the S&P 500 gave up at most 19% and was trading close to its peak again in September 2026. In both stress phases, Bitcoin amplified losses instead of cushioning them.

## Stablecoins

A [[stablecoin]] represents a dollar. The issuer promises to pay one dollar for it at any time and holds reserves for this purpose. The price hardly fluctuates, but the risk has not disappeared. Price risk is replaced by the creditworthiness and transparency of the issuer. There is no statutory deposit protection. Holders of a stablecoin are creditors of a company. Issuers authorised under the EU regulation MiCA (Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation) must hold the reserves separately from their own assets, so that other creditors cannot access them in the event of insolvency. The market is very highly concentrated.

bloecke.unter: Two issuers account for around 83% of the total supply. In practice, holders of stablecoins therefore bear credit risk towards very few debtors.

bloecke.md: TerraUSD was only algorithmically backed and therefore had no real backing. From 9 May 2022 the coin lost its peg to the dollar. Together with its sister token LUNA, around $45 billion in value was wiped out within a week. The previously advertised “return” of 19.45% in the Anchor protocol was paid out of reserves and not out of earnings. Even a coin with real backing can lose its peg. USDC lost it temporarily in March 2023 because part of its reserves was held at a bank that had run into difficulties. The peg ultimately held because the US authorities closed the bank but guaranteed all deposits, including those above the deposit insurance limit.

## Regulation and the digital euro

Two developments are running in parallel. The first is the regulation of private providers. The EU regulation MiCA (2023/1114) has applied to stablecoin issuers since 30 June 2024 and in full since 30 December 2024. The transitional period for existing providers ended EU-wide on 1 July 2026 at the latest, and in Germany as early as the end of 31 December 2025 (Section 50 of the Crypto Markets Supervision Act, KMAG). Since then, every crypto service provider in the EU has needed authorisation. This means that issuers, custodians and trading venues are supervised, but the price is not. An authorised provider may still sell a product that loses 80% in the following year.

The second is the digital euro, planned as central bank money for private individuals, that is as a claim directly on the ECB instead of on a commercial bank. Today, central bank money is available to citizens only as cash, and its share is small. In July 2026, currency in circulation of €1,613 billion compared with an M3 money supply of €17,614 billion. Around 84% of euro money is book money held at private banks. This gives rise to the debate about holding limits. An unlimited account at the central bank could drain deposits from banks in a crisis and accelerate a bank run instead of preventing it. The legislative process had not been completed in summer 2026. The digital euro has little in common with cryptocurrencies. According to the ECB's plans, it will be kept in a central ledger system of the Eurosystem; a blockchain is not envisaged for it. It is not scarce, not anonymous like cash and not intended as an investment.

punkte: The coins belong directly to the holder, and the insolvency of a third party cannot affect them.
Access depends on a seed phrase. If it is lost, the coins are lost, because there is no hotline and no reset. Heirs cannot get at them without it either.
The risk shifts from a provider's creditworthiness to your own diligence.
Convenient, with password reset and support. In the event of insolvency, the customer depends on the provider having kept the coins separate from its own assets, as MiCA requires.
Mt. Gox lost around 850,000 BTC in 2014, Celsius left $4.7 billion in liabilities to customers, and FTX misappropriated around $10 billion of customer funds.
MiCA authorisation improves supervision and the segregation of customer holdings, but is no substitute for deposit protection.

bloecke.unter: The collapses almost always affected the companies around the protocol and hardly ever the protocol itself.

The leading exchange at the time collapses in February; around 850,000 BTC have disappeared.

Approval on 10 January. In mid-September 2026 the largest product holds around $59.9bn with a fee of 0.25%.
The EU-wide transitional period ends on 1 July; in Germany it already ended on 31 December 2025. Since then, operating in the EU without authorisation has been unlawful.

bloecke.md:
The cases differ in how they unfolded, but follow the same pattern. Customer funds are held by the provider, the provider uses leverage, and customers are promised a fixed, conspicuously high return. Celsius advertised up to 17%, Anchor 19.45%, at a time when government bonds yielded almost nothing. In both cases these were payouts from reserves and from the money of customers who joined later, and not interest. The most useful check is therefore a commercial one rather than a technical one. The questions to clarify are who pays this return, what income it comes from and why it is so far above what the same issuer would have to pay on the bond market.

Where there is no company in between, the corresponding risk is called programming risk. In DeFi, that is decentralised finance applications, program code takes on the role of the institution, and with it, liability also disappears. The value locked in protocols was around $92 billion in September 2026, compared with $178 billion in November 2021. In 2025 alone, around $535 million was lost in at least 20 reported incidents. There, an error in the contract code takes effect immediately as a booking, and not only after a legal dispute.

The UCITS rules require diversification. A maximum of 10% is permitted per issuer, and all positions above 5% may together make up at most 40%. A fund on a single asset is therefore ruled out. This applies to Bitcoin just as much as to a single commodity. European products are therefore [[Exchange-traded note (ETN)|ETNs]] or ETPs, for example BTCE (DE000A27Z304). They are collateralised bearer bonds of the issuer and not segregated fund assets (Sondervermögen). If the issuer becomes insolvent, only the quality of the collateral counts. In the US, spot ETPs have been approved since 10 January 2024. They are not investment funds in the classic sense either.

Sales of crypto-assets held as private assets are private disposal transactions (private Veräußerungsgeschäfte) under Section 23 EStG (Income Tax Act). After a holding period of more than one year, gains are tax-free. Within one year, the personal income tax rate applies and not the flat-rate withholding tax (Abgeltungsteuer) of 25%. The limit of €1,000 is an exemption threshold (Freigrenze) and not an allowance (Freibetrag). With a gain of €999 no tax is due; with €1,000 the full amount is taxed. Every swap of crypto for crypto counts as a disposal and starts a new holding period. In the view of the tax authorities, ongoing staking income does not extend the holding period for cryptocurrencies such as Ether to ten years. This is set out in the circular of the Federal Ministry of Finance (BMF) of 10 May 2022 and in its revised version of 6 March 2025.

A portfolio of €100,000 has a crypto allocation of 5%, that is €5,000.

- If the pattern of 2018 repeats (−83%), around €850 remains. The loss of €4,150 corresponds to 4.2% of the total portfolio.
- If 2025/26 repeats (−53%), around €2,350 remains. The loss corresponds to 2.7% of the portfolio.

Both losses are unpleasant, but neither threatens your livelihood. With an allocation of 30%, they would be 25% and 16% of total wealth respectively. The question is then less about the level of the return than about whether you can still stay calm in the second year of the decline. Position size is the only variable in this calculation that can be reliably controlled.

The calculation also includes the way back, and it is not symmetrical. After a loss of 83%, a gain of 488% is needed to make up for it. At 77% it is 335%, and at 53% still 113%. Four cycles with declines of between 53% and 83% show that such crashes are not an exception for this asset and are part of its documented normal behaviour.

Shares, bonds and property are valued by discounting future payments such as dividends, coupons or rents. A crypto-asset pays nothing out. This means that not only is a particular model missing; in principle, no model of this kind can be built. There is no value against which a price could be judged “too high”. The price is determined solely by supply and demand.

The well-known substitute models do not stand up to scrutiny. The stock-to-flow model derives the price from the ratio of existing supply to new issuance and has failed formal out-of-sample tests. Network valuations along the lines of Metcalfe's law are regarded as spurious correlation. A 2026 review concludes that, over horizons of one to six months, no published model is reliably better than the naive benchmark according to which tomorrow's price will be roughly the same as today's.

Proof-of-stake networks at least offer an ongoing return. However, it comes mainly from new issuance and accrues in the same volatile unit. Such a return redistributes existing value and therefore cannot establish value.

Bitcoin is neither a fraud nor a substitute for money. It is software that has been running without interruption since 2009, with a credible supply rule, no income, no basis for valuation and about four times the volatility of an equity index. A holding in it is a speculation on future demand. Investors who enter into this speculation should size the position so that a fall of 80% does not affect their life plans. This condition is not a recommendation for or against a holding. Only once it is met can the question of a holding be asked in a meaningful way.

mitnehmen: Bitcoin's scarcity is based on a protocol rule and has largely already been reached. Around 95% has been mined, and the annual inflow is below 1% of the existing supply.
As money, Bitcoin does not fulfil the function of a unit of account, and it fulfils that of a store of value only with fluctuations that would be too large for a means of payment.
The diversification benefit is not stable. The correlation with equities rose from practically zero to around 0.45, and in the stress phases of 2022 and 2025/26 Bitcoin amplified the decline.
Stablecoins are promises to pay without deposit protection. MiCA governs the supervision of the providers, not the prices.
The big collapses all followed the same pattern of customer funds held in third-party custody, leverage and a promise of a fixed, high return.

begriffe.text: A ledger stored by all participants, whose blocks are chained together by cryptographic fingerprints. Subsequent changes are therefore noticed immediately.

Consensus mechanism in which computing work decides the right to append the next block. Security is paid for with electricity costs. Adjusting the difficulty keeps the block time at around ten minutes.

Consensus mechanism in which deposited coins instead of computing power secure validation. In the event of misconduct, part of the pledged deposit is lost. Ethereum switched to this method in 2022 and reduced its energy consumption by around 99%.
Halving of the Bitcoin block reward every 210,000 blocks, that is roughly every four years. The date has been known since 2009 and is therefore not a surprise supply event.

Crypto-asset that is meant to be pegged to a currency, usually the US dollar. Legally it is a promise to pay by the issuer without deposit protection. The risk lies in the backing and not in the price.

Exchange-traded bearer bond. Unlike a fund unit, it does not constitute segregated fund assets (Sondervermögen); if the issuer becomes insolvent, only the collateral counts. In Europe, crypto-assets are offered in this form because of the UCITS rules.
